IMPORTANT NOTE

After the SWEEP of the 9H high or low, Price action is allowed only ONE new low or high sweep

Exemples: 
Price sweeps 9H High. Goes down a bit, creates a new high, then displacement down, it's valid.

Price sweeps 9H High. Goes down a bit, creates a new high, goes down a bit from that new high, Creates a second high then displacement down, NOT VALID, it will go higher and you will get stopped.

Price needs MSS after ONE High/Low Sweep, after the hourly sweep

Best to all of you

Just tested this strategy on EURUSD
Setup - liquidity capture from the hourly candle 9:00.
Entry from 10-11 AM

Entry model - ICT 2022 - must be FVG. 
Targeting - 2R. 
Either stop or take profit.

comment_text:
Think of it as an outside bar. When price is moving upwards, an order block is the last up candle before a downward movement. But for it to be a valid order block, the high of that candle AND the low of that candle have to be taken by the next down candle. After this down candle, price will move down for a little while, but mark out the opening of that last up candle. When price comes back up and touches that opening price of that up candle, it will act as resistance, providing a possible entry to go short.

Same for downward price movement. Say that price is moving down, and then goes upward. The order block here would be the last down candle, before that upward movement. Remember though! This candle needs to have both its low and its high taken by the next candle, which is an up candle. Price will then move upwards, now mark the opening price of that last down candle which is the order block. When price comes back down, it may use this opening price level as support, possibly giving you a long position.

It’s not that difficult, people telling you how to trade makes it difficult. First of all, pick one equity to watch, spy, appl, nvda, forex pairs, whatever floats your boat. Watch how it behaves, Look for consistency. Don’t be watching 10 different tickers, you’ll get nowhere. Don’t be completely locked in on every candle, the market has weekly, monthly, yearly cycles, sometimes you’re better off not trading for a few days until the market gets out of it’s funk. When it starts moving that’s when you get active. That part of the cycle may only last for 3 days, depending on what’s going on. A good trader gives a signal at least 30 minutes to 1 hour before the trade is triggered, so everyone has a fair opportunity to enter at the same price level. It’s not about chasing trades or entering late.

Personally, I make 8% to 12% profit every month using proper risk management, and I will never charge anyone to help them learn how to trade. I believe in helping others grow, just as I did—without having to pay for basic knowledge.

Think wisely, and don’t fall for the hype.

Tržište često prvo pokaže laž, a tek onda pokaže svoju pravu namjeru. Cijena probija prethodni maksimum i privlači kupce, uzima stop-loss cijene prodavača, a zatim se vraća. Probija dno, uvjerava ljude da počinje pad, uzima likvidnost ispod njega i naglo mijenja smjer. Ljudi to nazivaju lažnim probojem, lovom na stop-loss ili manipulacijom, ali samo ime nije dovoljno. Slijed događaja je ono što je važno. Povlačenje likvidnosti nije automatski ulazak. Zona ponude ili potražnje nije automatski ulazak. Blok naloga, FVG, linija trenda, RSI, EMA ili bilo koja strelica nije automatski unos. Prvo moram znati gdje je likvidnost. Zatim čekam da cijena uzme tu poziciju, da se zatvori natrag, promijenim kratkoročnu strukturu kroz CHoCH ili BOS i tek se onda vraćam testirati mjesto odakle je krenuo pravi impuls. Bez tog lanca događaja, gledam samo oblik na grafikonu, a ne priču iza njega. Isto vrijedi i za vremenske okvire. Jedna minuta može se činiti savršenom za kupnju, dok petnaest minuta i jedan sat i dalje vode cijenu prema nižoj likvidnosti. Manji vremenski okvir ne treba promatrati kao zasebno tržište. On je samo detalj veće slike. Azijska sesija često gradi raspon i ostavlja likvidnost iznad i ispod njega. London može zauzeti stranu, napraviti snažan prvi potez ili postaviti zamku. New York tada može potvrditi London, vratiti se na svoj račun ili potpuno preokrenuti priču. Zato sat na grafikonu, prethodni dnevni i tjedni usponi i padovi te cjenovna pozicija unutar veće zone često znače više od nove obojene strelice. Kod EUR/USD, GBP/USD i zlata, dolar čak ni ne gledam zasebno. DXY mi daje kontekst, ali nije ni ulazni nalog. Ako je dolar u ključnoj zoni i samo uzima vlastitu likvidnost, signal na drugom instrumentu može imati potpuno drugačije značenje nego što se na prvi pogled čini. Najveća zabluda nije da tržište nema pravila. Zabluda je da se ta pravila mogu svesti na jednu liniju, prijelaz dvaju prosjeka ili postotak napisan pored signala. A još veća zabluda je da će vas dobar ulaz spasiti od lošeg upravljanja rizikom. Bez jasno definirane invalidacije, pravilnog stop-lossa i kontrole veličine pozicije, čak i ispravno čitanje tržišta može se pretvoriti u gubitak. Na ovom tržištu nema nepogrešive strategije niti zajamčene dobiti. Već dugo pokušavam sve dijelove spojiti u jednu logičnu cjelinu: likvidnost, lažni proboji, sesije, viši i niži vremenski okviri, DXY, bankarske zone, promjena strukture,povratak na posljednji nalog i upravljanje rizikom. Tek tada sam shvatio da prava razlika nije u tome tko ima više indikatora, nego tko razumije **što se mora dogoditi prije nego što kvalitetan ulaz uopće smije postojati**.
Najvažniji dio te priče nisam napisao u ovom komentaru, jer bez cijelog konteksta zvuči kao još jedna brza strategija. Složio sam ga u vlastitom priručniku, bez obećanja lake zarade i bez čarobnog signala. Tko ozbiljno proučava tržište i želi razgovarati o logici iza kretanja cijene, može mi se javiti

comment_text: Swing highs, Equal highs, & Trendlines hold huge liquidity same for lows. That’s why it’s best to only enter after the they get swept. When you see equal lows below Demand, place a limit order at the equal low. If you know price wicks equal lows then you have a safe systematic entry model. If price only taps the demand imbalance but doesn’t wick the equal, lows and continues to go bullish, then delete your order and come again tomorrow. It may not wick your entry in the trade a few times before hitting your TP but when it does, you’ll have the cheapest price to sell for a huge profit.

Waste of time. You need to feel the real markets in real time. It will teach you patience and quick decision making. Creating your strategy is easy once you know the basics, but creating a system and following your rules and risk management and demo forward testing it for a whole year while documenting every trade is the hard part. But it’s all worth it because the basics strategy you first practiced will slowly unwind itself into a big complex system that only you understand through out your Practice year on demo then it will all click toward the middle or end of the year. The simple strategy you first practiced will be your own personal system that you’ve created from adding on new confluences, from new information you’ve learned and experienced while trading. Believe me bro. That’s the only way to really be profitable. Then when you’ve got a whole years data showing you that you’re profitable, then you do it again on a live account for a year trading your finalised system sticking to your rules strictly. The live trading year is mainly a focus on your psychology and how you handle wins and losses trading your real money. If you ended that year sticking to your rules and profitable, that’s when you can get funded because you’ve proved to yourself you’re profitable. Don’t go live as a beginner looking to get funded. Believe me bro, in your first year as a beginner, you ain’t learned nothing yet😂😂. Experience will teach you what you need to know. Take your journey slow and steady. It’s not a race but a marathon. RETESTING THE EXTREME ZONE & THE LOGIC BEHIND BANK MOVEMENTS

The market didn’t revisit the extreme zone by accident—it returned to close a banking order that was positioned around the 50% mark of a wick. On the lower timeframes, we can spot liquidity within the wick, but on the higher timeframes, like the Daily, the story becomes clearer: the market shifted direction and formed a new Higher High (HH).

Here's the key: the market always pulls back to the last order that pushed it forward—the one that caused the recent HH or LL—before continuing the move. That’s why we must analyze higher timeframes first and then fine-tune entries on lower ones. Only when we combine both can we see the true narrative unfold.
